tests.name: MHPCO Claim Office quotes an empty item list as premium 5 G (processing fee only)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain sword as 115 G (100 G base + 10 G first insurance + 5 G fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain amulet as 71 G (60 G base + 6 G first insurance + 5 G fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain staff as 93 G (80 G base + 8 G first insurance + 5 G fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain potion as 49 G (40 G base + 4 G first insurance + 5 G fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single rune as 32.5 G (25 G base + 2.5 G first insurance + 5 G fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single moonstone as 32.5 G (25 G base + 2.5 G first insurance + 5 G fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a sword and an amulet as 181 G (160 G base + 16 G first insurance + 5 G fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 2 runes as base premium 50 G (no block) -- 60 G with surcharge and fee
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 3 runes as base premium 60 G (block applies) -- 71 G with surcharge and fee
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 4 runes as base premium 100 G (no block; block requires exactly 3) -- 115 G with surcharge and fee
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 7 runes as base premium 175 G (no block at 7) -- 197.5 G with surcharge and fee
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 2 runes + 1 moonstone as base premium 75 G (no block: different types) -- 87.5 G with surcharge and fee
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 3 runes + 3 moonstones as base premium 120 G (two separate blocks) -- 137 G with surcharge and fee
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 3 moonstones as base premium 60 G (block applies to moonstones too) -- 71 G with surcharge and fee
MHPCO Claim Office adds a 50 % curse surcharge on the cursed item's base premium: cursed sword => 100 + 50 + 10 + 5 = 165 G
MHPCO Claim Office adds a 30 % high-enchantment surcharge at enchantment exactly 5: sword => 100 + 30 + 10 + 5 = 145 G
MHPCO Claim Office adds no high-enchantment surcharge at enchantment 4: sword => 100 + 10 + 5 = 115 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies both curse and high-enchantment surcharges to a cursed sword with enchantment 5 => 100 + 50 + 30 + 10 + 5 = 195 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the curse surcharge only to the cursed item, not the policy total: cursed sword + plain amulet => 160 base + 50 curse + 16 first insurance + 5 fee = 231 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies a 20 % loyalty discount at exactly 2 years with MHPCO: sword => 100 - 20 + 10 + 5 = 95 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies no loyalty discount at 1 year with MHPCO: sword => 100 + 10 + 5 = 115 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 10 % first-insurance surcharge to a newcomer's first quote: sword, 0 years => 100 + 10 + 5 = 115 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 15 % follow-up-contract discount to a customer's second quote: sword, 0 years, second quote => 100 + 10 - 15 + 5 = 100 G

MHPCO Claim Office applies the first-insurance surcharge on every quote, regardless of customer history (each quoted item is a first insurance): 3-year customer's second quote on a plain sword => 100 + 10 - 20 - 15 + 5 = 80 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the loyalty discount to the policy base premium (sum of item base premiums), not per item: two swords, 2 years => 200 base - 40 loyalty + 20 first insurance + 5 fee = 185 G
MHPCO Claim Office rounds a premium of 197.5 G up to 198 G (MHPCO's favour)
MHPCO Claim Office keeps intermediate amounts fractional and rounds only the final premium: a single rune computes 32.5 G and is reported as 33 G
MHPCO Claim Office integration: newcomer (0 years, no previous contract) with a cursed steel sword (ench. 3) => premium 165 G
MHPCO Claim Office integration: 3-year customer's second quote with a cursed steel sword (ench. 7) => premium 160 G
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a quote containing an unknown item type (e.g. broomstick) by throwing an Error (CLI: non-zero exit, error on stderr, no results on stdout)
MHPCO Claim Office pays out 400 G for a regular steel sword (ench. 3) with damage 500 G (full reimbursement minus 100 G deductible)
MHPCO Claim Office pays out 100 G for a damaged rune (value 250 G) with damage 200 G (no enchantment or material => no special clause)
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 100 G deductible once per damaged item: sword 500 G + amulet 300 G in one incident => payout 600 G
MHPCO Claim Office reimburses 50 % for enchantment exactly 8: dragon sword ench. 8, damage 1000 G => payout 400 G
MHPCO Claim Office fully reimburses dragon material at enchantment 5: dragon sword, damage 800 G => payout 700 G
MHPCO Claim Office prefers the 50 % clause when both apply: dragon sword ench. 9, damage 1000 G => payout 400 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 50 % clause alone for a steel sword ench. 9, damage 1000 G => payout 400 G
MHPCO Claim Office never pays a negative amount: damage 50 G below the 100 G deductible => payout 0 G
MHPCO Claim Office caps a policy at twice the insurance sum: sword + amulet => insurance sum 1600 G, cap 3200 G
MHPCO Claim Office bases the cap on unmodified insurance values: cursed sword (premium 165 G) => cap 2000 G
MHPCO Claim Office counts each of two swords in the insurance sum: two swords => insurance sum 2000 G, cap 4000 G
MHPCO Claim Office ignores the block discount in the insurance sum: sword + 3 runes => insurance sum 1750 G, cap 3500 G
MHPCO Claim Office reports remainingCap after a claim: sword policy (cap 2000 G), claim 1500 G => payout 1400 G, remainingCap 600 G
MHPCO Claim Office limits a second claim to the remaining cap: second claim 1500 G => payout 600 G, remainingCap 0 G
MHPCO Claim Office treats two sword damage entries on a two-sword policy as separate damages with their own deductibles: 500 + 500 => payout 800 G
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim with more damage entries of a type than the policy covers (two sword damages, one sword insured) by throwing an Error (CLI: non-zero exit)
MHPCO Claim Office rounds a payout of 350.5 G down to 350 G (MHPCO's favour): ench. 8 sword, damage 901 G => 0.5 * 901 - 100 = 350.5
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim whose damaged item is not part of the policy (amulet damaged, only a sword insured) by throwing an Error (CLI: non-zero exit)
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim referencing an unknown item type by throwing an Error (CLI: non-zero exit)
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim with a negative damage amount (-200) by throwing an Error (CLI: non-zero exit)
MHPCO Claim Office CLI: reads the schema example scenario from stdin and writes {results:[{premium},{payout,remainingCap}]} to stdout
MHPCO Claim Office CLI: processes steps sequentially so a claim step resolves its policy by zero-based quote step index
MHPCO Claim Office CLI: exits with a non-zero status code and writes an error description to stderr for an invalid scenario, writing no results to stdout
